siding_surface_input_group.description: Rate per SF applies to net siding field area from PaintScope. Engine divides SF by rate to calculate hours.

task_production_rates.name: Landscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Deploy tarps along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent. ~30 sec per LF. Includes staking and securing tarps at grade line. LF-based — you measure the run along the house, not the area of the landscape beds.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Coverage adequate along working elevation. Minor gaps acceptable if no spray overspray risk.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full perimeter coverage of plantings within spray drift zone. Secure against wind.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete perimeter coverage secured at all edges. No gaps in protection.

task_production_rates.name: Hardscape Protection Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay drop cloths and plastic on flat surfaces. Faster than landscape. ~14 sec per SF.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Key areas covered. Minor gaps acceptable away from spray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Full coverage of walkways and patios within overspray zone.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage taped at edges. Non-slip canvas on crew traffic areas.

task_production_rates.name: Fixture and Utility Masking
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Bag and tape fixtures, utility panels, hose bibs. ~4 min per fixture. HVAC units take longer (~10 min).

defect_tolerance.QT3: Complete coverage. All fixtures and utilities fully masked.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Complete coverage with clean tape lines. Cover plates removed where accessible.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Configure airless sprayer, test tips (517 for lap/panel, 413 for shingle), run lines, stage materials (~45 min). Per elevation.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern on cardboard. Correct tip for profile.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Equipment calibrated. Test pattern verified at correct distance. Backup tips staged.

task_production_rates.name: Brush/Roll Equipment Setup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Stage brushes, rollers, trays, and access equipment (~20 min). Per elevation.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Fresh roller covers. Brushes in good condition.
defect_tolerance.QT4: New roller covers. Premium brushes. Materials pre-mixed.

task_production_rates.name: Low-Pressure Wash
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Garden hose + soft bristle brush. Faster than pressure wash — lower setup, no equipment staging. ~6 sec per SF. HIGH-PRESSURE POWER WASHING PROHIBITED on fiber cement.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All construction dust, dirt, and debris removed. Surface clean to touch.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Pristine surface. TSP solution wash. No residue. Allow 24-48 hr dry time.

task_production_rates.name: Scuff Sand for Adhesion
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 150-180 grit light scuff sand for adhesion profile. ~18 sec per SF. Required for factory-primed and factory-finished surfaces.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Light scuff pattern visible. Not removing material — creating tooth.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform scratch pattern across full surface. No missed areas.

task_production_rates.name: End-Seal Field-Cut Edges
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush end-cut sealer on each field-cut edge. ~50 sec per cut edge. Includes butt joints, miters, and field cuts.
task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Count of siding cut edges. Not captured by PaintScope — estimator enters count based on siding layout. Typical: 2-4 cuts per board for butt joints, window/door cutouts.

defect_tolerance.QT2: All cut edges sealed. Coverage adequate.
defect_tolerance.QT3: All cut edges sealed with full coverage. No bare cellulose visible.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All cut edges sealed. Inspect for completeness. Critical for FM-001 prevention.

task_production_rates.name: Caulk Siding-to-Trim Joints
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply and tool exterior paintable caulk at siding-to-trim joints. ~40 sec per LF. Do NOT caulk field butt joints on lap siding.
task_production_rates.manual_capture_notes: Linear feet of siding-to-trim joints requiring caulk. Includes corner board junctions, window/door casing junctions, frieze board junctions. Does NOT include field butt joints.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All siding-to-trim joints caulked. Smooth tool. No voids.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead. Precision tool smooth. Uniform appearance.

task_production_rates.name: Prep Dust Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Compressed air or tack cloth dust removal after sanding. ~6 sec per SF.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All sanding dust removed. Surface ready for primer.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Pristine surface. No visible dust. Tack cloth verification.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray primer on fiber cement siding. Factory-primed FC is less porous than bare wood — faster primer application. ~10 sec per SF. No backroll required.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays or thin spots.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. Full coverage. Inspect for holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Inspect under raking light at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Prime Coat — Brush/Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush for edges, roller for field. ~36 sec per SF. Same rate as wood siding brush/roll prime.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform coverage. Work primer into surface. Maintain wet edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform coverage with consistent roller texture. No lap marks.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray finish coat on primed fiber cement. NO back-rolling — spray only for factory-smooth surface. Base rate for lap_horizontal. ~12 sec per SF. Faster than wood siding spray+backroll (225 SF/hr) because no backroll pass.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Even coverage. No drips or holidays.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Uniform mil build. No visible spray pattern at 6 ft.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. No runs, sags, or curtaining.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush/Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush for edges, roller for field. Base rate for lap_horizontal. ~36 sec per SF. Fallback method for <750 SF, occupied adjacent, or high wind.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Consistent roller texture. No brush marks on field. Maintain wet edge.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform appearance. No lap marks, roller marks, or brush marks visible at 3 ft.

QT3.notes: Quick scan for obvious defects — runs, sags, holidays.

QT4.notes: Systematic inspection at 6 ft viewing distance. Mark all defects.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Note obvious runs, sags, holidays. Quick visual scan.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Systematic scan. All visible defects marked for repair.

task_production_rates.name: Interstage Light Sand
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 220 grit light scuff between finish coats. ~12 sec per SF. QT4 only.

defect_tolerance.QT4: Light uniform scuff. Remove nibs and defects. No deep scratches.

QT4.notes: Fix all found defects. Blend repairs.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Obvious defects repaired. No visible runs or holidays remain.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired and blended. Repairs invisible at 3 ft.

task_production_rates.name: Intercoat Dust Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth or compressed air dust removal after interstage sanding. ~6 sec per SF. QT4 only (paired with TSK_FCSD_SAND_BETWEEN).

defect_tolerance.QT4: All sanding dust removed. Surface clean for second finish coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Spray Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 spray. Primed surface is consistent. NO back-rolling.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

task_production_rates.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush/Roll Application
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Same rate as coat 1 brush/roll. Final coat.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Even coverage. No brush marks. Maintain wet edge. Final coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Uniform appearance. No defects visible at 3 ft. Final coat.

QT2.notes: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for misses.

QT3.notes: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance.

QT4.notes: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. 6 ft viewing standard.

defect_tolerance.QT2: No obvious misses or holidays visible from ground.
defect_tolerance.QT3: No defects visible at 6-10 ft from ground level.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No defects visible at 6 ft with binoculars. Coverage uniform across all elevations.

QT2.notes: Minimal touch-up. Fix obvious misses only.

QT4.notes: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly at 3 ft standard.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All noted defects repaired.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended seamlessly.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Material Removal
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all tarps, plastic, tape, fixture bags, HVAC covers along perimeter. ~18 sec per LF. Faster than setup — pull and fold vs. stake and secure.

defect_tolerance.QT3: All materials removed. No tape residue on surfaces.
defect_tolerance.QT4: All materials removed. Check for tape residue. Inspect for any paint on protected surfaces.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Equipment
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Flush airless sprayer, clean tips and filters, coil hoses. Clean brushes and rollers if used. ~30 min per session.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Full flush. Tips and filters cleaned.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Full flush cycle. Tips and filters cleaned and inspected. Equipment ready for next use.

task_production_rates.name: Site Debris Cleanup
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Collect debris (sandpaper, caulk tubes, tape, sealer containers, paint cans), dispose, final site walkthrough. ~20 min.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials removed.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Site restored. Walkthrough with customer. No evidence of work activity.

factor_modifiers.name: Access Type Height Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Access type drives production rate reduction for elevated work. Same concept as FAC_HEIGHT for interior.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applied per elevation. Ground tasks (end-seal, equipment setup, dust cleanup) are not affected — done at ground level or on sawhorses.

factor_modifiers.name: Siding Profile Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Siding profile dramatically affects application rate. Shingle is 2x due to many edges, complex geometry, constant repositioning.
factor_modifiers.notes: Lap is baseline (long horizontal runs). Panel slightly slower (fewer joints but large single runs require careful overlap). Shingle is dramatically slower — many overlapping edges, complex geometry, constant repositioning. Shingle 2.00x aligns with research range (spray: 300 SF/hr lap vs 100-150 SF/hr shingle).

factor_modifiers.name: Surface Texture Modifier
factor_modifiers.description: Textured profiles (cedarmill, roughsawn) require additional spray passes for DFT and slower production.
factor_modifiers.notes: Applies to BOTH production rate and material quantity (see coverage_profiles in materials.json). Textured profiles trap more paint in valleys, requiring additional passes for correct DFT.

quality_effects.notes: Economy tier. Single finish coat on primed surface. No interstage. Minimal inspection.
Standard tier. Two finish coats per Hardie warranty. Interstage inspection but no sanding.
Premium tier. Two finish coats. Light sand between coats. Systematic inspection at 6 ft. Premium materials.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Lap siding, smooth, ground access — baseline

modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Near worst case — under 4.0x stacking cap. ~78 SF/hr spray. Very slow but still fixed-price viable.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Shingle siding, roughsawn, scaffold access — maximum stack
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: EXCEEDS 4.0x stacking cap (4.16). Flag for review — recommend hourly billing for this combination. Shingle + roughsawn + scaffold is rare but possible.

modifier_stacking_examples.scenario: Lap siding, cedarmill, ladder access — common residential
modifier_stacking_examples.notes: Typical residential scenario. ~185 SF/hr spray — reasonable production.

assumptions: Base rates are for lap siding profile at ground access on smooth surface.
Profile, texture, and access modifiers stack multiplicatively: effective_rate = base_rate ÷ (profile × texture × access).
Modifier stacking cap: 4.0× maximum combined. Combinations exceeding 4.0x should be flagged for hourly billing.
NO spray/backroll coupling rule applies — fiber cement is spray-only (no back-rolling). This is a key departure from wood siding.
Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun, surface temp) are NOT estimation modifiers (RC-003 from wood siding sibling spec).
Spray finish rates (300 SF/hr) are higher than wood siding spray+backroll (225 SF/hr) because no backroll pass is needed.
Fiber cement primer spray rate (350 SF/hr) is higher than wood siding (200 SF/hr) because factory-primed FC is less porous than bare wood.
Shingle profile rates are conservative estimates pending field calibration.
risks: Shingle siding + roughsawn + scaffold exceeds 4.0x stacking cap (4.16x) — recommend hourly billing for this combination.
Shingle siding + brush/roll at any access level is very slow production (~50 SF/hr before texture modifier).
End-seal and caulk rates assume ground-level work or sawhorses.
HardieShingle production rates are extrapolated from wood shingle rates — flag for field calibration.
Factory-finished (ColorPlus) substrate requires scuff sand + bonding primer — estimator must verify substrate state before pricing.
validation_plan: Time 3 spray finish projects on lap siding at ground access to calibrate baseline 300 SF/hr.
Time 2 shingle profile projects to validate 2.0x profile modifier.
Compare fiber cement spray rates vs wood siding spray+backroll rates — expect FC to be 25-35% faster (no backroll pass).
Time cedarmill vs smooth production on same project to validate 1.20x texture modifier.
Track end-seal counts per project to develop estimating heuristic (cut edges per 100 SF of siding).
